### Important rules

Respect these finalized contracts:

* `POST /api/tickets` creates a ticket.
* `POST /api/tickets/list` performs listing/search/filtering using a JSON request body.
* List `page` is zero-based.
* API page `0` is displayed as page `1` in the UI.
* Default page = `0`.
* Default size = `20`.
* No backend maximum page size.
* `reporter`, never `reportee`.
* Search uses `searchKey`.
* `searchKey` null/omitted = no keyword filter.
* Search is case-insensitive substring matching against title and description only.
* Status has exactly six values.
* Status changes use the dedicated status operation.
* Field PATCH MUST NOT change status.
* Version starts at `1` and increments only after successful field/status updates.
* Stale version produces `STALE_VERSION` with no data/version change.
* CLOSED and CANCELLED are frozen except for REOPEN.
* Assignee cannot be cleared.
* Assignee must belong to the ticket's product.
* JWT TTL = 30 minutes.
* BCrypt is used for password hashing.
* Activity uses per-field JSON `from`/`to` maps containing changed fields only.
* Exactly one Activity document per successful field-update request.
* Exactly one Activity document per successful status change.
* Comments do not create Activity.
* API responses use `{ message, code, status, data }`.
* Login/authentication failures use `AUTHENTICATION_FAILED`.
* Backend i18n resolves response codes to messages.
* APIs expose DTOs only.
* JPA entities and Mongo documents must never be serialized directly.
* PostgreSQL owns users/products/memberships.
* MongoDB owns tickets/comments/activity.
* No distributed transaction.
* No Redis/Kafka/SSO/attachments/notifications/realtime functionality.

### Task quality requirements

For every task:

* Give it a unique task ID.
* Clearly identify whether it is backend, frontend, database, infrastructure, or test work.
* State the files/modules/components likely affected when supported by the plan.
* Include dependencies where necessary.
* Keep tasks small enough to implement and verify incrementally.
* Include tests with the relevant implementation work rather than leaving all testing until the end where practical.
* Ensure every functional requirement and acceptance scenario can be traced to one or more tasks.
* Include security and membership-isolation tests.
* Include state-machine transition tests for every allowed and rejected transition.
* Include optimistic-concurrency/stale-version tests.
* Include frontend no-submit validation tests.
* Include API contract/error-envelope tests.

Do NOT create implementation code.

After generating `tasks.md`, provide a traceability summary showing which task(s) cover each major functional area and identify any genuine missing coverage.
